statement: The bootstrap note scopes the first filesystem workflow on ecf/bootstrap-v1 and asserts it does not change the wire format or EAM semantics, yet it describes symlinks, POSIX mode, ownership, xattrs, hardlinks and sparse maps that posix-metadata-v1 adds as required incompatibility features.
refines_or_supersedes: Contradicted/extended by docs/posix-metadata-v1.md L3-7 (required feature 0x8000) and docs/security-metadata-v1.md L7-11 (0x10000)
research_needed: Documentation reconciliation: determine which statements of the bootstrap note remain normative vs historical.
decision_needed: Should filesystem-bootstrap.md be marked historical/superseded by the v1 fidelity documents?

statement: Packing accepts exactly one caller-selected directory and traverses it through held capability-directory handles.
research_needed: Usability evidence on whether single-root input suffices (multiple roots, file lists, stdin, single files).
decision_needed: Should v1 pack accept multiple roots, explicit file lists, or single-file inputs?

statement: Directory entries are sorted before traversal, and resulting Entries are then ordered and validated by EntrySet.
research_needed: Cross-platform determinism test: identical trees on Linux/macOS/Windows produce identical EntrySet order; specify sort key for native names.

statement: A regular file is opened once per attempt; its metadata and bytes come from that single handle, and length, mtime and executable status are rechecked on the same handle after reading.
research_needed: Fault-injection tests modifying files during pack.

statement: After the initial attempt, two fresh-handle retries are made; persistent change returns EB_INPUT_SOURCE_UNSTABLE.
evidence_in_source: none (numeric retry count chosen without cited measurement)
research_needed: Measure behavior on actively written files (logs, databases); evaluate whether 2 retries is adequate.
decision_needed: Should retry count be configurable, and should unstable files be skippable with a report instead of failing the whole pack?

statement: Stability is judged only by length, mtime and executable status on the same handle; modifications preserving these (same-size rewrite within mtime granularity, mmap writes, mode/owner/xattr changes) would not be detected as instability.
research_needed: Fault-injection experiment on coarse-mtime filesystems (FAT, SMB, ext4 with coarse timestamps) to quantify undetected inconsistent captures.
decision_needed: Should stability also compare ctime/change counters or re-hash content?

statement: Symlink metadata and exact target bytes are read without following the link, and traversal never descends through a symlink.
research_needed: Adversarial test trees with symlink loops and symlinks swapped for directories during traversal.

statement: Devices, FIFOs, sockets and other unsupported filesystem objects are rejected during packing; no special-file Entry kind exists.
research_needed: Survey backup/system-image workloads needing device nodes/FIFOs; compare tar/cpio behavior.
decision_needed: Should special files abort the pack, be skipped with a FidelityReport entry, or gain an Entry kind post-v1?

statement: All platforms capture core.mtime; supported Unix systems additionally capture core.executable, posix.mode, numeric uid/gid, xattrs and hardlink topology.
research_needed: Capture matrix test per OS/filesystem.

statement: Linux captures sparse layout using SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE and never infers holes from zero-filled content.
research_needed: Test on filesystems lacking SEEK_DATA support (which report whole file as data).

statement: Platform capabilities that cannot be observed reliably are declared unavailable in FidelityReport rather than fabricated.
research_needed: Audit every capture path for silent defaults (e.g., uid 0, mode 0644) on non-Unix platforms.

statement: The bootstrap note states ACLs, special-file semantics and other platform-specific metadata remain unavailable; this is stale for ACLs and platform metadata given the later platform fidelity feature.
refines_or_supersedes: Superseded by docs/platform-fidelity-v1.md L10-18, L32-33 (Linux POSIX ACL capture, Windows attributes/creation time, macOS flags/birthtime)
research_needed: Doc reconciliation against implementation.

statement: Normative POSIX metadata feature and extraction policy are delegated to posix-metadata-v1.md and filesystem-fidelity-v1.md.
New archives use normalized Gear-hash content-defined chunking; default balanced-v6 policy uses 128 KiB minimum, 512 KiB target, 2 MiB maximum Chunks.
evidence_in_source: none in this note (parameters cited without measurement here)
research_needed: Confirm chunking-v1.md provides corpus measurements justifying 128/512/2048 KiB for balanced.

statement: Exact SHA-256 Chunk deduplication is archive-wide.
research_needed: Memory cost of archive-wide dedup index at CLI limit of 4,000,000 Chunks.

statement: After dedup, a creation-only planner performs deterministic similarity analysis and compares independent multi-codec/structural pipelines against complete-cost shared-dictionary candidates.
refines_or_supersedes: Defined normatively in docs/planner-v1.md and docs/cross-file-compression-v1.md
evidence_in_source: description; no measurement in this note
research_needed: Determinism test across thread counts/platforms; benefit measurement of dictionary candidates.

statement: Dense and extreme profiles may select bounded ChunkGroups; the balanced profile never uses lookback.
research_needed: Measure random-access cost of ChunkGroups in dense/extreme.

statement: Each unique plaintext Chunk is encoded exactly once.
research_needed: Corpus check that no Chunk digest appears in two encoded frames.

statement: The reader uses only recorded plans, Dictionaries, groups and Chunk references; reading never depends on planner logic.
research_needed: Reader conformance test with planner code removed.

statement: Historical fixed-1mib/v1 and v2 archives remain readable.
research_needed: Retained historical archive corpus in CI.
decision_needed: How long must pre-release fixed-1mib/v1 and v2 archives remain readable, given they predate a stable v1 format?

statement: Chunking, planner and cross-file compression policies are delegated to chunking-v1.md, planner-v1.md and cross-file-compression-v1.md.
Extraction fully opens and verifies the archive and enforces caller resource policy before creating the destination root.
research_needed: Measure time/IO cost of full pre-verification on large archives.

statement: Full verification before any write implies extraction cannot stream from non-seekable input or begin output early; interaction with STREAM layout, remote access and very large archives is not addressed here.
research_needed: Measure extraction latency and peak resources for multi-GiB archives; evaluate verify-while-writing into staging.
decision_needed: Is a staged/streaming extraction mode (verify per object before commit) needed for v1?

statement: Extraction is described as creating the destination root; whether extraction into an existing directory (merge/overwrite) is supported, refused, or policy-controlled is not stated.
research_needed: Usability study of expected overwrite/merge behavior vs tar/unzip.
decision_needed: What are v1 semantics for extracting into an existing, non-empty directory?

statement: The destination root is held as a cap-std Dir, and each validated UTF-8 LogicalPath component is resolved relative to the held handle.
research_needed: Adversarial extraction corpus (path traversal, symlink races).

statement: LogicalPath components are UTF-8; handling of non-UTF-8 source filenames during Unix packing (refuse, escape, report) is not specified, although symlink targets may be POSIX_BYTES.
research_needed: Survey prevalence of non-UTF-8 names in real Unix trees; check current pack behavior.
decision_needed: Should non-UTF-8 source names be refused, losslessly represented, or recorded as lossy?

statement: Exclusive creation of distinct LogicalPaths on case-insensitive or normalization-insensitive destinations (NTFS, APFS, HFS+) and Windows-reserved names is not addressed; collisions would fail extraction.
research_needed: Cross-platform extraction test with case/normalization collisions and CON/NUL names.
decision_needed: What is the v1 policy for destination-native name collisions and reserved names?

statement: Extraction creates directories and representative files exclusively, then hardlink siblings, then symbolic links last.
Default Safe symlink policy accepts only relative targets whose lexical resolution stays beneath the root; Refuse and explicit All are also available.
research_needed: See lexical-vs-physical resolution question.

statement: Ownership, xattr and sparse restoration are caller-controlled choices.
Ownership is applied before final mode, directory metadata after descendants, and timestamps last.
Any metadata that cannot be restored is returned in ExtractionReport.
CLI bootstrap policy permits at most 1,000,000 entries and 4,000,000 distinct Chunks.
research_needed: Measure memory at limits; survey real trees (node_modules, source monorepos, maildirs) exceeding 1M entries.
decision_needed: Are these CLI limits final v1 defaults, and can users raise them via flags?

statement: CLI bootstrap policy permits at most 64 GiB total logical bytes and 16 GiB for a single file.
research_needed: Usability evidence: backups, VM images and datasets commonly exceed 16 GiB files / 64 GiB totals.
decision_needed: Should the CLI default logical-byte limits be raised or made streaming-proportional for v1?

statement: CLI bootstrap policy permits path depth up to 1,024 and 1 GiB for the manifest/metadata bound.
research_needed: Measure manifest size per entry with rich metadata; relate 1 GiB to 1M entries with xattrs/ACLs.

statement: An archive declaration exceeding caller policy is POLICY_REFUSED; decoded actuals exceeding the archive's own declaration are corruption.
research_needed: Negative conformance vectors for both cases.

statement: Applications embedding the library should choose resource limits suitable for their environment.
decision_needed: Should the library ship a safe default ResourceBudget or require callers to supply one?

statement: Archives additionally declare a 1 MiB Zstandard decoder window or up to an 8 MiB LZMA2 dictionary, plus an aggregate working-set requirement covering codec state, stored Dictionaries and maximum bounded-group access.
research_needed: Measure ratio cost of 1 MiB zstd window / 8 MiB LZMA2 dictionary caps versus larger windows.
decision_needed: Clarify wording: are window and dictionary declarations per-codec alternatives or both declared?

statement: The CLI permits an aggregate decoder working set up to 384 MiB so a declared v6 JPEG reconstruction working set can be honored.
evidence_in_source: none (limit chosen to fit JPEG reconstruction; no measurement cited)
research_needed: Measure actual JPEG reconstruction peak memory; evaluate on low-memory devices.
decision_needed: Is 384 MiB an acceptable default decoder memory ceiling for v1 CLI?

statement: Caller policy enforces window/dictionary and working-set limits before section decoding and can be narrowed by an embedding application.
research_needed: Fuzz declarations to confirm enforcement precedes allocation.

statement: Status: POSIX filesystem fidelity is implemented for Unix capture and restoration, with explicit capability reporting on other platforms.
research_needed: Verify against code/tests on Linux and macOS.

statement: Archive validity and extraction safety are separate: an archive may be valid yet refused or partially restored by extraction policy.
Traversal uses held capability directories and no-follow type/metadata calls.
A source symlink is captured as an Entry and is never traversed or opened as its target.
Unix symlink target bytes are taken from the native OsStr representation.
Regular files and directories capture executable flag, nanosecond mtime, mode & 0o7777, numeric uid/gid and accessible xattrs.

Capture metadata is enumerated only for regular files and directories; which items (mtime, uid/gid, xattrs) are captured for Symlink Entries is not stated, though symlink ownership/timestamps are later called capture-only.
research_needed: Inspect implementation and document symlink metadata capture set.
decision_needed: Which metadata items are captured and stored for Symlink Entries?

statement: Only 'accessible' xattrs are captured; whether inaccessible attributes or namespaces (e.g., trusted.*, permission-denied reads) are silently skipped or reported in FidelityReport is unspecified.
research_needed: Test unprivileged capture of files with trusted.* and security.* xattrs.
decision_needed: Must inaccessible xattr namespaces be reported as FidelityReport limitations?

statement: Xattr path operations are no-follow; an enumerated attribute that disappears or fails unexpectedly is a source-instability/capture failure, never silent omission.
Unix (device, inode) pairs are only temporary traversal evidence for detecting multiply linked regular files.
Hardlink group IDs are finalized only after canonical paths and ContentObject digests are known; inode values never enter output bytes or any identity root.
research_needed: Determinism test: same tree copied to different filesystems yields identical bytes.

statement: Every hardlink alias is stability-checked, and inode-scoped metadata must agree across aliases.
Handling of a multiply linked file whose other links lie outside the packed root (only one alias captured) is not stated; group rules require at least two members.
research_needed: Test pack of subtree containing single alias of nlink>1 file.
decision_needed: Is a lone alias captured as an ordinary File silently or with a FidelityReport note?

statement: Linux sparse discovery uses SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE and records the returned data extents instead of guessing from zero runs.
When filesystem sparse behavior is unsupported, the sparse map is omitted and a typed FidelityReport limitation added; logical bytes are always captured.
research_needed: Determine how 'unsupported' is detected, since filesystems without SEEK_DATA support report the whole file as data rather than failing.

statement: Sparse discovery is described only for Linux; other platforms (macOS, BSDs, Windows) report unavailable POSIX classes rather than capturing sparse layout.
research_needed: Feasibility of safe-Rust sparse discovery on macOS/FreeBSD (SEEK_HOLE) and Windows allocated-range queries.
decision_needed: Is non-Linux sparse capture needed for v1?

statement: Other platforms report unavailable POSIX metadata classes instead of fabricating values.
Production POSIX dependency xattr 1.6.1 (MIT/Apache-2.0) provides no-follow xattr operations.
research_needed: Dependency longevity and unsafe-code audit of xattr crate.

statement: Production dependency rustix 1.1.4 (Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT) provides safe Unix fchown and Linux sparse seeks.
research_needed: Dependency longevity review.

statement: Entrybound adds no unsafe code for POSIX fidelity; unsafe platform access is delegated to audited dependencies.
research_needed: Audit unsafe blocks in xattr/rustix/cap-std for no-follow correctness.

statement: ExtractionPolicy symlink choice: Refuse, Safe (default), or All.
ExtractionPolicy ownership choice: Ignore (default) or Restore.
ExtractionPolicy xattr choice: Ignore (default) or Restore; macOS FinderInfo/ResourceFork/quarantine therefore are not restored by default.
evidence_in_source: description plus inference from docs/security-metadata-v1.md L137-138
research_needed: Usability evidence on macOS: does default Ignore lose user-visible data (resource forks, Finder tags)?
decision_needed: Should xattr restoration default differ per platform?

statement: ExtractionPolicy sparse choice: Logical (default) or Restore.
Canonical ACL and Windows/macOS extraction policy controls extend this ExtractionPolicy list in platform-fidelity-v1.md.
No policy control exists for posix.mode or timestamps; whether setuid/setgid/sticky bits are restored by default for unprivileged extraction, and whether umask applies, is unspecified.
research_needed: Security review comparing tar/bsdtar default setuid stripping; test current behavior.
decision_needed: Should setuid/setgid/sticky restoration require explicit opt-in?

statement: Safe symlinks require a relative target whose lexical resolution from the link's parent stays beneath the extraction root; absolute, drive/rooted and escaping targets are refused without rewriting the archived target.
Lexical resolution can diverge from physical resolution when a target traverses another archived symlink (e.g., d/s -> '..' then t -> 'd/s/..'); both pass lexically yet t physically escapes the root.
research_needed: Adversarial symlink-chain corpus against Safe policy; compare with physical resolution within the created tree.
decision_needed: Must Safe resolve targets through already-archived symlinks rather than lexically?

statement: All is the explicit opt-in for exact absolute or escaping symlink targets.
The extractor fully verifies the archive before creating final objects.

Extraction order: create directories and hardlink representatives, write file content or declared sparse extents, create remaining hardlinks, apply directory metadata deepest to shallowest, then create symlinks last.
Because symlinks are created last, an archive-created symlink can never redirect a later extraction write.
research_needed: Security test including concurrent local attacker modifying destination during extraction, pre-existing symlinks in destination, and Windows junctions.

statement: Ordering is ambiguous: directory metadata (restrictive mode, timestamps) is applied before symlinks are created last, while timestamps are also said to be last; creating symlinks afterwards would perturb parent directory mtimes and fail in non-writable directories.
refines_or_supersedes: Same ambiguity in docs/platform-fidelity-v1.md L55-58 (timestamps last, symlinks last) and docs/filesystem-bootstrap.md L41-46
research_needed: Test extraction of read-only directory containing a symlink; check restored directory mtime.
decision_needed: What is the single normative extraction ordering including symlinks vs parent directory metadata?

statement: Ownership is applied before final permission bits because chown may clear setuid/setgid.
Xattrs are applied through file descriptors or no-follow symlink operations.
Timestamps are applied after operations that would otherwise mutate them.
Restrictive directory permissions are delayed until descendants exist.
Sparse Restore truncates to the full logical size and writes only declared data extents; Logical writes the complete byte sequence.
research_needed: Verify extents are physically sparse after restore on ext4/xfs/btrfs/APFS/NTFS.

statement: Every skipped or failed metadata operation appears in ExtractionReport rather than being described as restored.
Symlink ownership and no-follow symlink timestamp restoration are reported capture-only where the portable safe API cannot guarantee them.
research_needed: Survey safe Rust APIs for lchown/utimensat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) on Linux/macOS.

statement: Symlink ownership/timestamps are runtime capture-only, yet MetadataItem-v2 fixes restorability to Restorable and has no CaptureOnly value, so the stored flag can misstate restorability.
refines_or_supersedes: Tension with docs/posix-metadata-v1.md L53-56 and docs/security-metadata-v1.md L39-41
decision_needed: Is restorability a stored per-item fact or a runtime capability, and should v2 items on Symlinks be encoded differently?

statement: Ownership restoration can require privilege.
On Windows extraction, only UTF-8 symlink targets are accepted and symlink creation may require platform symlink privilege.
research_needed: Measure fraction of Windows users lacking symlink privilege (Developer Mode off).

statement: Windows symlinks must be created as file or directory links; how the type is chosen for dangling, forward or later-created targets is not specified.
research_needed: Test extraction of dangling and directory-targeting symlinks on Windows.
decision_needed: How is the Windows symlink file/directory flag determined and recorded?

statement: POSIX_BYTES symlink target capture and full POSIX metadata restoration are Unix-only.
Behavior when extracting on Windows an entry with POSIX_BYTES target, mode, uid/gid or xattrs (whole-extraction failure vs per-entry skip with report) is not specified.
research_needed: Cross-platform extraction test matrix.
decision_needed: Is a non-representable symlink target a per-entry refusal or a whole-extraction failure?

statement: Status: native POSIX metadata v1 is implemented.
The document freezes the semantic and canonical wire contract selected by required incompatibility feature 0x8000 (posix-metadata-v1).
research_needed: Independent-reader implementation from this document alone.

statement: Feature 0x8000 is present exactly when an archive contains a Symlink Entry or any metadata name 3-8.
research_needed: Negative vectors: feature set without such content and content without feature must both be rejected.

location: posix-metadata-v1.md §Native POSIX metadata v1 (status) L5-6; posix-metadata-v1.md L112-113
statement: Because feature 0x8000 is set exactly when symlinks or POSIX metadata exist, cleartext feature bits of an encrypted archive may reveal that such content is present, despite private-manifest confidentiality.
research_needed: Check whether feature bits are authenticated-but-cleartext in encrypted archives; threat-model assessment.
decision_needed: Should encrypted archives hide or always-set content-dependent feature bits?

statement: Archives without feature 0x8000 retain the historical Entry and MetadataItem version-1 bytes and identity results.
research_needed: Historical identity digest regression corpus.

statement: Native Entry kinds are a closed set: Directory, File and Symlink.
refines_or_supersedes: Extended by docs/security-metadata-v1.md L17-18 (ReparsePoint kind 4 under feature 0x10000)

statement: A File has exactly one internal ContentObject digest; a Directory has no content; a Symlink has no ContentObject and exactly one LinkTarget.
LinkTarget encoding registry: UTF8 (ID 1) when target bytes are valid UTF-8; POSIX_BYTES (ID 2) when they are not.
Symlink targets are opaque, bounded to 1 MiB, and may not contain NUL.
evidence_in_source: none (1 MiB bound without cited rationale)
research_needed: Compare with PATH_MAX and Windows reparse target limits; confirm bound is enforced before allocation.

statement: The phrase 'nonempty-or-empty' leaves unclear whether an empty symlink target is valid; Linux and macOS generally refuse creating empty symlink targets.
research_needed: Check implementation acceptance of empty targets and extraction behavior.
decision_needed: Is an empty LinkTarget canonical, and how is it extracted?

statement: Link targets are not LogicalPaths: '/', '..' and absolute targets are valid archive semantics; extraction policy separately decides whether creating the link is safe.
UTF-8 target bytes encoded as POSIX_BYTES are noncanonical.
research_needed: Negative vector for UTF-8 bytes tagged POSIX_BYTES (absent from vectors file).

statement: LAI inputs: path, kind, File ContentObject digest, Symlink target encoding and bytes, and core.executable.
research_needed: Identity digest vectors computing real LAI for File and Symlink Entries.

statement: AUX inputs: core.mtime, posix.mode, ownership, hardlink topology, xattrs and sparse layout.
research_needed: AUX digest vectors.

statement: None of the POSIX metadata enters PCR solely by existing; exact container serialization remains PCI.
research_needed: Property test: metadata-only changes with fixed physical plan leave PCR unchanged.

location: posix-metadata-v1.md §Entry model and identity L25-28; posix-metadata-v1.md L69-71
statement: Since core.executable is LAI but posix.mode is AUX, and executable must agree with mode only when both exist, an Entry with mode but no executable item could produce a different LAI for identical semantics.
research_needed: Check whether writers/readers require core.executable whenever posix.mode is present.
decision_needed: Must core.executable be present whenever posix.mode is present on a File?

statement: Entry stays canonical record type 3; version 2 fields in strictly increasing tag order: 1 path components, 2 kind u8, 3 digest, 4 target encoding, 5 target bytes, 6 MetadataItem-v2 sequence, 7 identity digest, 8 AUX digest.
Entry-v2 cardinality: Directory omits tags 3-5; File has tag 3 and omits 4-5; Symlink omits 3 and has 4-5; no kind is inferred from absence.
research_needed: Negative vectors for each cardinality violation.

statement: Entry-v2 must contain a Symlink or a metadata-v2 name 3-8, so an old Entry cannot acquire a second canonical form.
Each Entry must use the lowest record version able to express it, so Entry-v1, v2 and v3 records necessarily coexist within one feature-bearing archive.
research_needed: Conformance vector with mixed Entry versions in one manifest.

statement: Entry v1 remains byte-for-byte unchanged.

location: posix-metadata-v1.md §Entry record v2 L42; posix-metadata-v1-vectors.txt L6-7
statement: Tag 6 cardinality is not stated; the ENTRY_V2_SYMLINK vector encodes tag 6 as a present empty sequence, so whether omitting tag 6 is noncanonical must be specified.
research_needed: Negative vector with tag 6 omitted.
decision_needed: Is the metadata sequence tag always required even when empty?

statement: Every MetadataItem nested in Entry-v2 uses record version 2, including historical names 1 (core.executable) and 2 (core.mtime).
MetadataItem-v2 requires tags 1-3: name u8, criticality u8 fixed at 0 (Optional), restorability u8 fixed at 1 (Restorable); exactly one typed value field follows.

All v2 (and listed v3) metadata is fixed Optional criticality, so the criticality field carries no information; when, if ever, Critical metadata is permitted and how readers must treat it is undecided.
research_needed: Identify metadata whose loss must fail extraction (e.g., encryption attributes, immutable flags).
decision_needed: What is the role of Critical metadata criticality in v1?

statement: MetadataItem name registry: 1 core.executable (bool), 2 core.mtime (Timestamp), 3 posix.mode (u32), 4 posix.uid (u32), 5 posix.gid (u32), 6 posix.hardlink-group (bytes32), 7 posix.xattrs (XAttrV1 seq), 8 posix.sparse-map (SparseMapV1).
core.mtime is stored as bytes containing one canonical Timestamp type-9 record.
research_needed: Timestamp range/precision canonicalization vectors (none in vectors file).

statement: Only mtime (plus Windows creation time and macOS birthtime) is represented; atime, ctime and Linux statx birth time are not captured or modelled.
research_needed: Survey backup/forensic workflows needing atime/btime; compare tar/pax and 7z.
decision_needed: Should Linux birth time or atime be representable in v1?

statement: posix.mode may contain only bits 0o7777; file-type bits are never stored in mode.
MetadataSet is uniquely keyed and ordered by numeric name ID.
If posix.mode and core.executable are both present, executable must equal (mode & 0o111) != 0.
research_needed: Negative vector for disagreement.

statement: Hardlinks are ordinary File Entries referencing the same ContentObject plus one group digest; equal files lacking the digest are not hardlinks.
Every hardlink group has at least two members, identical inode-scoped metadata, and each Entry has at most one membership.
research_needed: Negative vectors: singleton group, divergent metadata, conflicting digests.

statement: The set of 'inode-scoped metadata' that hardlink aliases must share (mode, uid, gid, mtime, xattrs, sparse map, ACLs, platform flags, executable) is not enumerated.
research_needed: Extract the comparison set from implementation and freeze it in the spec.
decision_needed: Which metadata names are inode-scoped for hardlink agreement?

statement: Hardlink group ID is the structured hash with domain 'entrybound/hardlink-group/v1' over the shared ContentObject digest and a count-prefixed, length-framed, canonically sorted LogicalPath sequence.
research_needed: Vector for hardlink group digest computation (absent from vectors file).

statement: Readers recompute the hardlink group digest from the complete EntrySet.

Group validation needs the complete EntrySet; behavior under metadata-first random access, STREAM reads, and selective extraction of only some group members (whether hardlinks are formed among selected members) is unstated.
research_needed: Test selective extraction and random metadata reads on archives with hardlink groups.
decision_needed: How are hardlink groups validated and materialized for partial reads/extraction?

statement: Because the group digest covers member paths, renaming or adding one alias changes the AUX of every member, which may inflate diff and incremental-change reports.
research_needed: Diff experiment renaming one hardlink alias.
decision_needed: Is path-derived group identity acceptable for diff/incremental semantics?

statement: Device and inode numbers are traversal evidence only and are never serialized.
XAttrV1 is record type 37 version 1: tag 1 exact name bytes, tag 2 exact value bytes.
Xattr names are nonempty, NUL-free, at most 255 bytes, sorted by raw bytes, and unique.
Xattr values are at most 16 MiB, an Entry has at most 4096 xattrs, and empty and binary values are valid.
evidence_in_source: none (bounds without cited measurement); ENTRY_V2 vector has empty and binary values
research_needed: Compare with platform maxima (Linux 64 KiB VFS limit, macOS resource fork sizes, Windows EAs) and worst-case manifest size.

statement: Xattr values are stored inline in the manifest rather than as deduplicated ContentObjects, so large macOS ResourceForks count against the metadata budget and gain no Chunk dedup or content compression.
research_needed: Measure manifest growth on macOS trees with resource forks and large xattrs.
decision_needed: Should large xattr values be stored as content objects?

statement: Generic inspection reports only xattr name, length and SHA-256 of the value.
research_needed: Privacy analysis: unsalted SHA-256 of low-entropy values is guessable; confirm inspection is not considered confidentiality.

statement: Under feature 0x10000, Linux system.posix_acl_access and system.posix_acl_default values are projected into the canonical ACL model and not duplicated in posix.xattrs; all other accessible xattrs remain exact.
refines_or_supersedes: Refined by docs/security-metadata-v1.md L65-107 and docs/platform-fidelity-v1.md L10-14

statement: Archives without feature 0x10000 keep the v2 interpretation, in which POSIX ACL xattrs remain exact posix.xattrs.

Behavior when a Linux POSIX ACL xattr cannot be projected (malformed, unknown tag, unsupported version) under feature 0x10000 is not stated: exact xattr retention, capture failure, or FidelityReport limitation.
research_needed: Fuzz kernel ACL xattr parser; test malformed values set by root.
decision_needed: What happens to unprojectable ACL xattrs?

statement: All other accessible xattrs remain exact, including security.capability, security.selinux and system.nfs4_acl; restoring them under xattrs Restore is a privilege-bearing, dangerous-restoration decision not addressed.
research_needed: Security review of xattr namespaces that grant privilege; compare tar/bsdtar defaults.
decision_needed: Should privilege-bearing xattr namespaces require a separate opt-in on restore?

statement: SparseMapV1 is type 38 v1 (tag 1 logical size u64, tag 2 ordered SparseExtentV1 sequence); SparseExtentV1 is type 39 v1 (tag 1 offset u64, tag 2 nonzero length u64).
Sparse extents are in range, strictly ordered, nonoverlapping and nonadjacent; adjacent extents must be merged.
research_needed: Negative vectors for adjacency, overlap, out-of-range.

statement: Bytes outside sparse extents are holes and must be zero in the authoritative ContentObject.
research_needed: Verify readers check hole bytes are zero and measure verification cost on large sparse files.

statement: A sparse map is valid only on a File and has at most 1,000,000 extents.
research_needed: Measure extent counts of fragmented VM/database images.

statement: It is not explicitly stated that SparseMapV1 logical size must equal the ContentObject logical length.
research_needed: Negative vector with mismatched logical size.
decision_needed: Require logical size equality explicitly?

statement: The ContentObject always remains the sole full logical-byte authority; sparse maps are auxiliary layout.
Since holes are stored as zero bytes in the ContentObject, packing very large sparse files reads and chunks the holes, relying on zero-Chunk dedup for size and time efficiency.
research_needed: Measure pack time and archive size for mostly-empty VM images under CDC.
decision_needed: Should capture avoid reading declared holes?

statement: Fixed per-object bounds combine with caller-owned ResourceBudget.max_metadata_bytes, entry count, logical-byte and decoder limits.
Canonical sequence framing and checked arithmetic are applied before semantic construction.
research_needed: Fuzzing of Entry/Metadata decoder with adversarial counts and lengths.

statement: INDEXED, STREAM, encrypted private manifests, metadata-first random access, representation-only/replanned repack, diff, inspect and explain all use the same Entry/Metadata decoder.
research_needed: Code audit confirming no parallel decoders.

statement: Encrypted archives reveal none of the Entry/metadata private manifest material before authentication.
research_needed: External security review of observable sizes, feature bits and section lengths in encrypted archives.

A present security.acls item holds one to three ACLs, each with 1-65,536 ACEs, and (dialect, scope) pairs are unique.

statement: AclEntryV1 is type 41: type tag 1/u8, principal tag 2/u8, optional numeric ID tag 3/u32, optional UUID tag 4/bytes16, permissions tag 5/u32, flags tag 6/u32; types ALLOW=1, DENY=2, AUDIT=3, ALARM=4.
ACL principal registry: 1 USER_OBJ, 2 USER (uid), 3 GROUP_OBJ, 4 GROUP (gid), 5 MASK, 6 OTHER, 7 OWNER@, 8 GROUP@, 9 EVERYONE@, 10 UUID (16 bytes).

Principal validity per dialect is not stated for NFS4 (e.g., whether USER_OBJ, MASK or OTHER are allowed), and principals are only numeric IDs or UUIDs, so name-based NFSv4 principals (user@domain) and Windows SIDs are unrepresentable.
research_needed: Survey NFS4 ACL producers (FreeBSD, ZFS, NFS clients) for principal forms; negative vectors per dialect.
decision_needed: Which principals are valid in NFS4 ACLs, and are named principals needed?

statement: POSIX1E ACEs are ALLOW with zero flags and permissions limited to READ=0x1, WRITE=0x2, EXECUTE=0x4.
POSIX1E canonical order is USER_OBJ, named USER by uid, GROUP_OBJ, named GROUP by gid, MASK, OTHER; USER_OBJ, GROUP_OBJ and OTHER occur exactly once and MASK exactly once iff named entries exist.
research_needed: Negative vectors including duplicate named uid/gid entries (uniqueness not explicitly stated).

statement: NFS4 ACLs preserve semantically significant ACE order.
NFS4 accepted permission registry is ACE4_* mask 0x001f01ff (read/write/append data, named attrs, execute, delete child, read/write attributes, delete, read/write ACL, write owner, synchronize).
research_needed: Check mask against RFC 7530/8881; NFSv4.1 retention bits (e.g., 0x200, 0x400) fall outside and would be rejected.

statement: NFS4 accepted inheritance/ACE flag mask is 0x000000ff: file/directory inherit, no-propagate, inherit-only, successful/failed-access audit, identifier-group, inherited.

research_needed: Assess forward-compatibility cost: new registry bits would require a new feature version.

statement: A POSIX1E ACCESS ACL requires posix.mode; USER_OBJ, effective group class (MASK if present, else GROUP_OBJ) and OTHER must equal the owner, group and other mode classes.
